segments.label: §3 source sentence 1
segments.text: Es darf daher wohl mit Recht ein Bedürfniss für die allgemeine Sprachkunde genannt werden, die Amerikanischen Sprachen in ihrem Zusammenhange zu betrachten, ihren Bau zu erforschen, darzustellen, und mit dem Bau der Sprachen der übrigen Welttheile zu vergleichen.

segments.label: §3 source sentence 2
segments.text: Dies nach meinen Kräften, in gehöriger Vollständigkeit, vorzüglich aber mit so tief, als möglich, in das Wesen dieser Sprachen eindringenden Forschung zu thun, ist meine Absicht bei der gegenwärtigen Schrift.

segments.label: §3 source sentence 3
segments.text: Um dieselbe zu erreichen, habe ich eine Reihe von Jahren hindurch die einzelnen Sprachen nicht bloss studirt, sondern selbst bearbeitet, und seit noch längerer Zeit Materialien, vorzüglich handschriftliche, gesammelt.

segments.label: §3 source sentence 4
segments.text: Dass das Sammeln dieser Art nie Vollständigkeit erreichen kann, liegt in der Natur der Sache selbst.

segments.label: §3 source sentence 5
segments.text: Aber die Hülfsmittel, die mir zu Gebote stehen, und die als Quellen für diese Untersuchung anzusehen sind, bieten, verbunden mit dem schon in mehreren andren Werken sehr zweckmässig Vorgearbeiteten, einen reichlichen Stoff zu einer, das ganze Feld dieser Untersuchung umfassenden Bearbeitung, und einen hinreichenden zu einer sichren Beurtheilung dar.

segments.label: §3 claude rendering 1
segments.text: It may therefore well be called, with justice, a need of the general study of language to consider the American languages in their interconnection, to investigate and set forth their structure, and to compare it with the structure of the languages of the other parts of the world.

segments.label: §3 claude rendering 2
segments.text: To do this according to my powers, with due completeness, but above all with an investigation that penetrates as deeply as possible into the essential nature of these languages, is my intention in the present work.

segments.label: §3 claude rendering 3
segments.text: In order to achieve this intention, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but worked them up myself, and for a still longer time I have collected materials, chiefly manuscript ones.

segments.label: §3 claude rendering 4
segments.text: That collecting of this kind can never attain completeness lies in the very nature of the matter.

segments.label: §3 claude rendering 5
segments.text: But the resources that are at my disposal, and that are to be regarded as the sources for this investigation, offer, when combined with the preparatory work already very serviceably done in several other works, abundant material for a treatment embracing the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a secure judgment.

segments.label: §3 muse rendering 1
segments.text: It may therefore surely be called rightly a need for the general study of language to consider the American languages in their interconnection, to investigate their structure, to present it, and to compare it with the structure of the languages of the other parts of the world.

segments.label: §3 muse rendering 2
segments.text: To do this as far as my powers allow, with due completeness, but above all with inquiry penetrating as deeply as possible into the nature of these languages, is my intention in the present work.

segments.label: §3 muse rendering 3
segments.text: In order to attain that intention, I have for a series of years not merely studied the individual languages, but myself worked on them, and for a still longer time have collected materials, chiefly manuscript materials.

segments.label: §3 muse rendering 4
segments.text: That collecting of this kind can never attain completeness lies in the nature of the matter itself.

segments.label: §3 muse rendering 5
segments.text: But the resources that are at my disposal, and that are to be regarded as sources for this investigation, offer, in combination with what has already been very fitly prepared in several other works, abundant material for a treatment encompassing the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a secure judgment.

segments.label: §3 codex rendering 1
segments.text: It may therefore reasonably be called a need of general linguistic inquiry to consider the American languages in their interrelations, to investigate and describe their structure, and to compare it with the structure of the languages of the other parts of the world.

segments.label: §3 codex rendering 2
segments.text: My intention in the present work is to do this to the best of my abilities, with due completeness, but above all through inquiry that penetrates as deeply as possible into the nature of these languages.

segments.label: §3 codex rendering 3
segments.text: To achieve this intention, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but also worked on them myself, and for an even longer time have collected materials, especially manuscripts.

segments.label: §3 codex rendering 4
segments.text: That collecting of this kind can never attain completeness follows from the very nature of the undertaking.

segments.label: §3 codex rendering 5
segments.text: But the resources at my disposal, which are to be regarded as sources for this investigation, together with the very useful preparatory work already done in several other works, provide ample material for a treatment encompassing the entire field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a sound assessment.

segments.label: §3 synthesis rendering 1
segments.text: It may therefore rightly be said that the general study of language calls for considering the American languages in their interconnection, investigating and describing their structure, and comparing it with that of the languages of the other parts of the world.

segments.label: §3 synthesis rendering 2
segments.text: My intention in the present work is to do this to the best of my abilities, with due completeness, but above all through inquiry that penetrates as deeply as possible into the nature of these languages.

segments.label: §3 synthesis rendering 3
segments.text: To achieve this aim, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but also worked on them myself, and for an even longer time collected materials, chiefly in manuscript.

segments.label: §3 synthesis rendering 4
segments.text: Collecting of this kind can never be complete; that follows from the nature of the undertaking itself.

segments.label: §3 synthesis rendering 5
segments.text: But the resources at my disposal, which are to be regarded as the sources for this investigation, together with the very useful preparatory work already done in several other works, provide abundant material for a treatment covering the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a sound assessment.

segments.label: §3 revised rendering 1
segments.text: It may therefore well be said, with good reason, that the general study of language calls for considering the American languages in their interconnection, inquiring into and describing their structure, and comparing it with that of the languages of the other continents.

segments.label: §3 revised rendering 2
segments.text: My intention in the present work is to do this to the best of my abilities, with due completeness, but above all through inquiry that penetrates as deeply as possible into the essential character of these languages.

segments.label: §3 revised rendering 3
segments.text: To achieve this aim, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but also prepared my own treatments of them, and for an even longer time collected materials, chiefly in manuscript.

segments.label: §3 revised rendering 4
segments.text: Collecting of this kind can never attain completeness; that is inherent in the nature of the matter itself.

segments.label: §3 revised rendering 5
segments.text: But the resources that are at my disposal and are to be regarded as sources for this investigation provide, when combined with what has already been very usefully prepared in several other works, abundant material for a treatment covering the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a reliable assessment.

decision.authority: coordinator under D014; English review pending
decision.question: Discipline, comparative scope and qualifications
decision.resolution: Retain the qualified claim about the needs of general language study, interconnection and structure; use continents consistently without asserting a common original language.

decision.authority: coordinator under D014; English review pending
decision.question: Aim and depth of inquiry
decision.resolution: Preserve personal ability, due completeness and above-all priority; render Wesen as essential character locally, distinguishing Natur.

decision.authority: coordinator under D014; English review pending
decision.question: Study versus own treatment; manuscript resources
decision.resolution: Preserve the contrast between studying and personally preparing treatments and the longer collecting period. Do not invent completed grammars, fieldwork or autograph-only manuscripts.

decision.authority: coordinator under D014; English review pending
decision.question: Limits of collecting
decision.resolution: Preserve the impossibility of completeness and its inherence in the matter itself; the semicolon does not add an independent causal premise.

decision.authority: coordinator under D014; English review pending
decision.question: Sources, prior work and adequacy
decision.resolution: Keep source resources distinct from the earlier work combined with them. Preserve abundant versus sufficient material and repeat the elided noun in English.

decision.question: The hedging particle 'wohl' is not rendered, and the nominal predication 'ein Bedürfniss … genannt werden' is recast as 'the general study of language calls for'. The sense survives, but the German is a hedged claim about what may justly be called a need; the English is slightly more direct and makes the discipline the agent.
decision.resolution: Restore well and the explicit good-reason qualification; retain a readable calls-for recasting without claiming a stronger obligation.

decision.question: 'the general study of language' for 'die allgemeine Sprachkunde' can be read as studying language in a general way, not as the named field. It also uses singular 'language', where the context is the comparative knowledge of languages. Unresolved alternative: 'general linguistics' is clearer as a discipline name but arguably anachronistic for Humboldt; 'general study of languages' is the more literal option.
decision.resolution: Retain the established general study of language; no modern disciplinary boundary is imposed. Singular language names the field rather than changing the plural languages under investigation.

decision.question: Two renderings are defensible but not the only readings. (a) 'in their interconnection' for 'in ihrem Zusammenhange' fixes the sense as mutual relations among the languages; the German also allows 'as a connected whole'. The end of §2 (large traits of similarity across all American languages, no real North/South boundary) supports either. (b) 'parts of the world' for 'Welttheile' is literal, but the period sense is 'continents', as 'des Welttheils' in §2 shows.
decision.resolution: Use continents consistently with §§1–2. Keep interconnection, noting connected-whole as an alternative and avoiding a common-origin inference.

decision.question: 'Wesen' (s2) and 'Natur' (s4) are both rendered 'nature', which erases a lexical distinction in the source. The two words are not used contrastively against each other here, so no claim is distorted. A smaller instance of the same kind: 'Schrift' (s2) and 'Werken' (s5) both become 'work(s)'.
decision.resolution: Use essential character for Wesen locally and nature for Natur. Keep present work for Schrift without inventing a specific publication genre.

decision.question: 'worked on them myself' is weak for 'selbst bearbeitet' and blurs the 'nicht bloss … sondern' contrast, since studying a language is already working on it. 'Bearbeiten' here means working the languages up or elaborating them, which matches the opening of §4 on his own grammars and dictionaries. Unresolved alternative: after 'nicht bloss … sondern', 'selbst' can be the intensifier 'even' ('but even worked them up') and not the reflexive 'myself'. Both readings are grammatical; the translation silently chooses 'myself'. The added 'also' is harmless.
decision.resolution: Use prepared my own treatments to preserve active scholarly working-up beyond studying. Do not specify completed grammars/dictionaries; record the possible scalar selbst.

decision.question: Attachment ambiguity created in English. In the German, 'verbunden mit dem … Vorgearbeiteten' comes after the finite verb 'bieten', so it modifies the main clause: the resources, combined with the earlier work, provide the material. In the English, 'together with the very useful preparatory work' directly follows the relative clause 'which are to be regarded as the sources for this investigation', so it can be read as saying the earlier work is also to be regarded as sources. That blurs the source's distinction between his own 'Hülfsmittel' as 'Quellen' and what others have already worked out.
decision.resolution: Place the combined-with adjunct after provide so it plainly modifies provision of material, not the relative clause about sources.

decision.question: Three small shifts. (a) 'the sources' adds a definite article the German lacks ('als Quellen'), implying these are the sole sources. (b) 'very useful preparatory work' turns the adverb of manner 'sehr zweckmässig' (work done very purposively or serviceably) into an adjective of utility; 'preparatory work … done in several other works' also repeats 'work' awkwardly and may suggest those works were merely preparatory. (c) The two coordinated relative clauses ('die mir zu Gebote stehen, und die … anzusehen sind') are rendered asymmetrically, the first as a restrictive phrase and the second as a non-restrictive clause. German punctuation does not settle restrictiveness, so a fully restrictive reading ('those aids at my disposal that count as sources') remains open.
decision.resolution: Remove the added definite article before sources, restore parallel relative clauses, and use very usefully prepared rather than treating the other works themselves as merely preparatory.

decision.question: Cross-sentence vocabulary. 'Investigat-' covers both 'erforschen' (s1) and 'Untersuchung' (s5, twice), while 'Forschung' (s2) becomes 'inquiry'. So the erforschen/Forschung word family is split and one of its members is merged with 'Untersuchung'. Nothing is misstated, but the echo of §2's 'tiefer eindringenden Forschung' in s2 depends on how §2 is rendered. Separately, 'the nature of the undertaking' (s4) narrows 'Natur der Sache' ('the matter itself') slightly; this is acceptable.
decision.resolution: Use inquiring/inquiry for the local erforschen/Forschung echo; retain investigation for Untersuchung. Restore matter itself in sentence4.

decision.question: “May rightly be said that … calls for” drops the modal qualifier “wohl” and recasts a “Bedürfniss für” the discipline as the discipline itself calling for something, slightly shifting modality and agency.
decision.resolution: Restore well and the explicit good-reason qualification; retain readable indirect predication rather than a stiff nominal calque.

decision.question: Rendering “Wesen” as “nature” uses the same English word later used for “Natur” in p3:s4, obscuring a German terminological distinction. Whether “Wesen” requires the more technical “essence” cannot be settled from the supplied packet alone.
decision.resolution: Use essential character for Wesen locally, distinguishing Natur without freezing essence as a universal glossary rule.

decision.question: “Worked on them myself” weakens “selbst bearbeitet”: the German indicates his own working-up or elaboration of the languages, not merely effort expended on them, and that sense also connects with “Bearbeitung” in p3:s5.
decision.resolution: Strengthen to prepared my own treatments and qualify its scope in a note.

decision.question: “Can never be complete; that follows from the nature of the undertaking” turns attaining “Vollständigkeit” into a state, changes “liegt in” into an inference, and narrows the generic “Sache” to an “undertaking.”
decision.resolution: Restore attaining completeness, inherence and matter itself; retain the semicolon as an English sentence-structure choice.

decision.question: “The sources” adds definiteness and possible exhaustiveness not expressed by the bare plural “als Quellen.”
decision.resolution: Use sources without an added definite article; no claim of exhaustiveness is introduced.

decision.question: “Sound assessment” shifts “sichren Beurtheilung” from a secure or reliable judgment toward one that is well-founded in quality.
decision.resolution: Use reliable assessment to preserve epistemic reliability rather than suggesting absolute certainty; judgment remains a defensible alternative.

text_version.body: Es darf daher wohl mit Recht ein Bedürfniss für die allgemeine Sprachkunde genannt werden, die Amerikanischen Sprachen in ihrem Zusammenhange zu betrachten, ihren Bau zu erforschen, darzustellen, und mit dem Bau der Sprachen der übrigen Welttheile zu vergleichen. Dies nach meinen Kräften, in gehöriger Vollständigkeit, vorzüglich aber mit so tief, als möglich, in das Wesen dieser Sprachen eindringenden Forschung zu thun, ist meine Absicht bei der gegenwärtigen Schrift. Um dieselbe zu erreichen, habe ich eine Reihe von Jahren hindurch die einzelnen Sprachen nicht bloss studirt, sondern selbst bearbeitet, und seit noch längerer Zeit Materialien, vorzüglich handschriftliche, gesammelt. Dass das Sammeln dieser Art nie Vollständigkeit erreichen kann, liegt in der Natur der Sache selbst. Aber die Hülfsmittel, die mir zu Gebote stehen, und die als Quellen für diese Untersuchung anzusehen sind, bieten, verbunden mit dem schon in mehreren andren Werken sehr zweckmässig Vorgearbeiteten, einen reichlichen Stoff zu einer, das ganze Feld dieser Untersuchung umfassenden Bearbeitung, und einen hinreichenden zu einer sichren Beurtheilung dar.

text_version.body: It may therefore well be called, with justice, a need of the general study of language to consider the American languages in their interconnection, to investigate and set forth their structure, and to compare it with the structure of the languages of the other parts of the world. To do this according to my powers, with due completeness, but above all with an investigation that penetrates as deeply as possible into the essential nature of these languages, is my intention in the present work. In order to achieve this intention, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but worked them up myself, and for a still longer time I have collected materials, chiefly manuscript ones. That collecting of this kind can never attain completeness lies in the very nature of the matter. But the resources that are at my disposal, and that are to be regarded as the sources for this investigation, offer, when combined with the preparatory work already very serviceably done in several other works, abundant material for a treatment embracing the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a secure judgment.

text_version.body: It may therefore surely be called rightly a need for the general study of language to consider the American languages in their interconnection, to investigate their structure, to present it, and to compare it with the structure of the languages of the other parts of the world. To do this as far as my powers allow, with due completeness, but above all with inquiry penetrating as deeply as possible into the nature of these languages, is my intention in the present work. In order to attain that intention, I have for a series of years not merely studied the individual languages, but myself worked on them, and for a still longer time have collected materials, chiefly manuscript materials. That collecting of this kind can never attain completeness lies in the nature of the matter itself. But the resources that are at my disposal, and that are to be regarded as sources for this investigation, offer, in combination with what has already been very fitly prepared in several other works, abundant material for a treatment encompassing the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a secure judgment.

text_version.body: It may therefore reasonably be called a need of general linguistic inquiry to consider the American languages in their interrelations, to investigate and describe their structure, and to compare it with the structure of the languages of the other parts of the world. My intention in the present work is to do this to the best of my abilities, with due completeness, but above all through inquiry that penetrates as deeply as possible into the nature of these languages. To achieve this intention, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but also worked on them myself, and for an even longer time have collected materials, especially manuscripts. That collecting of this kind can never attain completeness follows from the very nature of the undertaking. But the resources at my disposal, which are to be regarded as sources for this investigation, together with the very useful preparatory work already done in several other works, provide ample material for a treatment encompassing the entire field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a sound assessment.

text_version.body: It may therefore rightly be said that the general study of language calls for considering the American languages in their interconnection, investigating and describing their structure, and comparing it with that of the languages of the other parts of the world. My intention in the present work is to do this to the best of my abilities, with due completeness, but above all through inquiry that penetrates as deeply as possible into the nature of these languages. To achieve this aim, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but also worked on them myself, and for an even longer time collected materials, chiefly in manuscript. Collecting of this kind can never be complete; that follows from the nature of the undertaking itself. But the resources at my disposal, which are to be regarded as the sources for this investigation, together with the very useful preparatory work already done in several other works, provide abundant material for a treatment covering the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a sound assessment.

text_version.body: It may therefore well be said, with good reason, that the general study of language calls for considering the American languages in their interconnection, inquiring into and describing their structure, and comparing it with that of the languages of the other continents. My intention in the present work is to do this to the best of my abilities, with due completeness, but above all through inquiry that penetrates as deeply as possible into the essential character of these languages. To achieve this aim, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but also prepared my own treatments of them, and for an even longer time collected materials, chiefly in manuscript. Collecting of this kind can never attain completeness; that is inherent in the nature of the matter itself. But the resources that are at my disposal and are to be regarded as sources for this investigation provide, when combined with what has already been very usefully prepared in several other works, abundant material for a treatment covering the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a reliable assessment.
